title: Drop when the ball is free
titleKid: Free player on the ball? Step back
brief: Their #8 is finding space between your midfield and your back line.
briefKid: Their midfielder is finding space in front of your defenders.
question: Their #8 has turned and nobody is pressing. What does your back line do?
questionKid: Their midfielder turned, and nobody is near them. What do you do?

takeaway.standard: When the player on the ball is facing forward with nobody pressing them, the back line drops a few metres together: they can see the pass in behind, so take that space away.
takeaway.kid: If their player has time to look up, take a few steps back together.

misconceptions.text: You held your line with nobody pressing the ball, so one pass over the top puts their runner through on goal.
misconceptions.textKid: They have time to pass behind you. Take a few steps back.

misconceptions.text: You stepped out toward the ball and left a hole in the back line behind you; drop with your line instead.
misconceptions.textKid: Stay in your line and step back with your defenders.
